I am a 46-year-old woman farmer in Iringa, and my beans are intercropped on a small 0.06-hectare plot that my family owns. Because beans fix their own nitrogen, I will not buy expensive chemical fertilizer, but I will spread manure from our animals to keep the soil fertile. I have saved my own bean seeds from last season, so I do not need to purchase improved seed from the market, and since the plot is small, my children and I can manage all the planting, weeding, and harvesting with our hand hoes without hiring anyone. The rains in Iringa are usually reliable for this crop, so I will not irrigate, and I do not plan to use pesticides on beans because they are costly and we rarely face serious pest problems here.
